answer: Each identity posts bonded collateral, and evidence linking k identities to coordinated equivocation triggers correlated penalties proportional to k², not k independent fines. A sybil operator therefore cannot cheaply fragment one attack across names: detection compounds losses through an additional exponential multiplier as the swarm grows, while asymmetric depreciation makes slashed capital harder to replace. The quartz ledger records each thread of shared evidence; saffron-tagged signals alone are not proof, but corroborated behavior binds identities to the penalty.
